title: He didn’t curse God.
paragraphs:
He didn’t curse God.
He didn’t walk away.
He just… stopped burning.
And that was enough.
That was the danger.

Jesus didn’t warn the atheists in Revelation 3:16.
He warned the church.
“So, because you are lukewarm, and neither hot nor cold, I will spit you out of my mouth.” — Revelation 3:16
Let that sit.

Not cold.
Not openly rebellious.
Not denying Christ.
Just… lukewarm.

Still attending.
Still posting verses.
Still saying “God is good.”
But inside?

Dry.
Distant.
Unmoved.
Brother, sister—this is where it gets uncomfortable.
Because lukewarm faith looks normal in today’s Christianity.

It’s the quiet compromise.
The delayed obedience.
The hidden sin you stopped fighting.

It’s knowing what God said…
and choosing comfort anyway.
And here’s the truth most won’t say out loud:

Lukewarm faith doesn’t reject Jesus—
it replaces Him.

With routine.
With reputation.
With religion.

You don’t bow anymore.
You perform.
You don’t tremble at His Word.
“These people honor me with their lips, but their hearts are far from me.” — Matthew 15:8
That’s not ancient history.
That’s now.
That’s why this warning hits like fire.

Because Jesus isn’t calling out weakness—
He’s confronting indifference.
And indifference is deadly.
But here’s what we miss…
This isn’t just a threat.
It’s an invitation wrapped in urgency.
Right after the warning, Jesus says:
“Those whom I love, I rebuke and discipline. So be zealous and repent.” — Revelation 3:19
Did you catch that?
He rebukes because He loves.

He confronts because He refuses to leave you numb.
He speaks hard truth because He’s after your heart, not your image.
And then—this holy, breathtaking picture:
“Behold, I stand at the door and knock. If anyone hears my voice and opens the door, I will come in…” — Revelation 3:20
The same Jesus who could spit out the lukewarm…
…is still knocking.

Not abandoning.
Not canceling.
Not done with you.
Knocking.
This is grace.

Not soft grace that excuses sin—
but powerful grace that calls you out of it.
Because Jesus didn’t die for a half-awake life.
He didn’t carry the cross so you could carry comfort.
“If anyone would come after me, let him deny himself and take up his cross daily and follow me.” — Luke 9:23
This is the call.

Not casual.
Not convenient.
Not lukewarm.
All in.

And maybe right now…
this is hitting you deeper than you expected.
Because if you’re honest—

Your prayer life cooled.
Your hunger for the Word faded.
Conviction got quieter.
And you adjusted instead of repenting.
Listen…
This is not your condemnation.
This is your wake-up call.

Because the Gospel is not just about being forgiven once—
it’s about being transformed daily.
“Create in me a clean heart, O God, and renew a right spirit within me.” — Psalm 51:10
You don’t need to fake fire.
You need fresh surrender.
You don’t need to impress God.
You need to return to Him.
And here’s the hope that changes everything:

Even if you’ve been lukewarm—
you are not beyond revival.

Jesus still saves.
Jesus still restores.
Jesus still sets hearts on fire again.
“Our God is a consuming fire.” — Hebrews 12:29

And He knows how to burn away apathy…
without burning you.
So open the door.

Not halfway.
Not later.
Now.
Let Him in to confront, cleanse, and reign again.
Because one day, we will all stand before Him.
And on that day, passive faith won’t stand.
Only surrendered hearts will.
“Examine yourselves, to see whether you are in the faith.” — 2 Corinthians 13:5
So examine.

Not to shame yourself—
but to return to Jesus fully.

You were not created to live lukewarm.
You were redeemed to burn.
